before:
County Herbarium — Mounting Queue Catalogue

The catalogue lists all unmounted sheets held in the north annexe, grouped by accession year and by collector. Bench time is limited to two afternoons a week, so the queue is worked in a settled order: brittle fern material is mounted ahead of loan-bound specimens, and loan-bound specimens ahead of duplicate grass sheets. Nothing is excluded from the queue on this account; every sheet in the annexe is mounted eventually, and the annual return counts them all the same. Volunteers write the date of mounting in the right-hand column and initial the entry. Sheets found with insect damage go to the freezer cabinet for a fortnight before they reach the bench at all.

before:
Fell Bothy Association — Notice to Overnight Users, Kilnbrae

The bunk room sleeps six and is allocated on arrival, with walkers arriving on foot given the bunks first and late parties taking the floor of the main room. Cyclists may bring machines into the porch overnight. Water is drawn from the beck above the gate; the tap in the yard is not potable between November and March. Fuel left in the bin belongs to whoever needs it, and users are asked to replace what they burn before leaving. The visitor book is kept on the sill, and the association asks that every party sign it, including those who stop only for shelter during the day.
after:

before:
Municipal Baths, Greyfield Road — Attendant's Handbook, Section 4

Section 4 covers the changing rooms and the locker bank on the pool side. Attendants walk the aisles at the top of each hour and again at closing, checking that doors are shut and that no clothing has been left on the benches. If you find a locker jammed, tell the duty supervisor straight away. Keys handed in at the desk are logged against the locker number and held for twenty-eight days before going to the lost property cupboard. Wet towels left in the drying racks overnight are laundered on Thursdays. Anything found in the pockets of abandoned clothing is bagged, labelled with the date, and kept in the office safe.

before:
Inland Fisheries Board — Annual Report Extract, Bailiff Activity

Bailiffs walked the lower river on ninety-one occasions during the year, most often in the evenings of late summer. The board's byelaw of 1974 forbids angling within twenty metres of the mill sluice, and the extract sets out how often that stretch was checked. Eleven verbal warnings were given, of which two led to written reports; no prosecutions were brought. Water levels were low from June until the second week of September, and three fish kills were reported above the weir, two of them attributed to a slurry discharge traced to Coldharbour Farm. The bailiff rota, which lost two members in the spring, is to be advertised again in the new year.

before:
Upland Seed Bank — Accession Drying Process

Incoming collections are weighed on receipt and given a temporary number. The bags are then opened in the sorting room, cleaned of chaff on the sieve bench, and moved to the drying cabinet at fifteen degrees. Once the moisture meter reads below six per cent the seed is counted into vials, and the vials are labelled and photographed before going to the cold store. Any collection failing the germination test is held back in the annexe and the collector told by letter. The cabinet book is signed at each transfer. Nothing may enter the cold store without a completed accession sheet, and the sheets are filed in the office cabinet under the year of collection.

before:
Fenland Drainage Board — Register of Contributory Charges

The register lists every holding in the district with its area, its band, and the sum due for the year. Charges are worked out from the 1962 acreage schedule, applying the band multiplier to the area in the second column. Sums under five pounds are not collected but remain on the register as a note. The clerk issues demands in April and reminders in July; unpaid sums after October are referred to the board's solicitor. Holdings that change hands are amended on production of the conveyance, and the register is closed to amendment for the fortnight before the annual meeting. A copy is kept at the pumping station office for inspection during working hours.

before:
Blackmoss Reservoir — Keeper's Manual, Part 2

Throughout this part, top water level means the overflow lip at the northern spillway, taken as the datum for every gauge reading in the manual. Drawdown, freeboard and the flood allowance in Part 3 are all expressed as distances below it, and the keeper's daily board is marked from the same zero. Readings are taken at eight each morning from the stilling well and entered in the book with the wind direction. Where the reading falls more than four metres below datum the keeper telephones the engineer, and where it stands above it for two consecutive days the low-level draw-off is opened. The gauge plate was last re-painted in the spring.
after:
Blackmoss Reservoir — Keeper's Manual, Part 2

Throughout this part, top water level means the crest of the earth embankment at its lowest surveyed point, taken as the datum for every gauge reading in the manual. Drawdown, freeboard and the flood allowance in Part 3 are all expressed as distances below it, and the keeper's daily board is marked from the same zero. Readings are taken at eight each morning from the stilling well and entered in the book with the wind direction. Where the reading falls more than four metres below datum the keeper telephones the engineer, and where it stands above it for two consecutive days the low-level draw-off is opened. variation_site: The change falls in the opening sentence of Part 2.
author_note: Moves the datum that every later figure in the manual is expressed against, so the change ripples; it reads like a fact about the reservoir, which is the trap.

Members will have noticed the new lighting over the marine tank, paid for from the raffle. The winter survey of the tidal pools at Redcarr counted twenty-eight shore crabs, four of them berried, and no sign of the spiny starfish seen the previous year.
